rows.citation: Song, Z., Liu, Y., Wan, C., et al. (2026). Your Simulation Runs but Solves the Wrong Physics: PDE-Grounded Intent Verification for LLM-Generated Multiphysics Simulation Code. arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.09360.
rows.model_type: PDE-based multiphysics simulation input files (MOOSE Kernels/BCs), plus static checks on UFL/FEniCS, FreeFEM, FiPy, Devito; not neuroscience
rows.controlled_mutations: partial: 30 MOOSE-executed perturbation pairs (structural, boundary-value, coefficient edits) used to validate the metric; not a systematic single-fault operator family
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: verification reconstructs the encoded PDE and compares it structurally to an intended contract; no stimulus or input battery
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: structural Intent Fidelity Score and coefficient-matching score plus final-field relative L2 error; no electrophysiology
rows.protocol_optimization: no: optimises generated code via an error-guided refinement loop, not selection of test inputs or protocols
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: cross-DSL static generalisation and cross-model contract transfer reported; no discovery/held-out split for selecting tests
rows.ai_transformations: yes: code generated by several LLMs (e.g. Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, DeepSeek V4 Flash) and repaired by LLM refinement loops
rows.software: moose-ifs https://github.com/HaningZS/moose-ifs (MIT per GitHub API; includes IFS metric and 220-case MooseBench)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares the motivating claim that executable, converging simulation code can be scientifically wrong. It verifies symbolic PDE structure against intent; NeuroSem instead detects behavioural divergence via multi-protocol electrophysiology fingerprints with calibrated tolerances, single-fault mutants, battery selection and held-out models. Also notes coefficient errors can evade structural checks, which behavioural testing targets.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API api.datacite.org/dois/10.48550/arxiv.2605.09360 (title, 7 creators, 2026, abstract); arXiv abs page arxiv.org/abs/2605.09360 citation meta tags (submitted 10 May 2026, v1); arXiv HTML full text arxiv.org/html/2605.09360 (methods, perturbation experiment, LLMs, code link); GitHub REST API repos/HaningZS/moose-ifs (license MIT)
rows.found_via: DataCite API (arXiv DOIs) title query LLM + simulation code; abstract via DataCite

rows.citation: Gleeson, P., Crook, S., Cannon, R. C., et al. (2010). NeuroML: A Language for Describing Data Driven Models of Neurons and Networks with a High Degree of Biological Detail. PLoS Computational Biology, 6(6), e1000815.
rows.model_type: conductance-based single-compartment, morphologically detailed and network neuron models in NeuroML v1.x (XML), run on NEURON, GENESIS, MOOSE, PSICS and others
rows.controlled_mutations: no: models converted to NeuroML and compared across simulators; no deliberate faults injected
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: somatic current injections/pulses and synaptic inputs used to compare simulators, but no systematic per-model stimulus battery
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: membrane-potential traces compared across simulators; no standardised feature-extraction set or numeric tolerances evident in full text
rows.protocol_optimization: no: no selection or optimisation of stimulation protocols
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: demonstration of cross-simulator convergence, not a held-out evaluation design
rows.ai_transformations: no: manual conversion and simulator export; no AI-generated transformations
rows.software: NeuroML language and tooling (current documentation https://docs.neuroml.org, listed as homepage in NeuroML GitHub repository metadata)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Its cross-simulator behavioural comparison is an early translation-equivalence check, and it reports convergence only at fine spatial/temporal discretisation, motivating refinement-based tolerance calibration. NeuroSem would add controlled single-fault mutants, a multi-protocol eFEL feature fingerprint with frozen tolerances, battery selection and held-out evaluation.

rows.citation: Cannon, R. C., Gleeson, P., Crook, S., et al. (2014). LEMS: a language for expressing complex biological models in concise and hierarchical form and its use in underpinning NeuroML 2. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 8.
rows.model_type: LEMS/NeuroML 2 hierarchical XML models: ion channels, synapses, point and conductance-based neurons, networks; also systems-biology models
rows.controlled_mutations: no: language and tooling description; no fault injection
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: illustrative simulations with current-clamp input and brief current pulses; not a testing battery
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: example voltage and gating traces shown; no feature extraction or tolerance-based comparison
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: no evaluation design of a testing method

rows.citation: NeuroML organisation (2014). pyNeuroML [software; GitHub repository; latest release v1.3.22 on PyPI and Zenodo, 2026]. GitHub.
rows.model_type: NeuroML2/LEMS cell and network models (tooling for reading, writing, simulating, analysing)
rows.controlled_mutations: no: no mutation operators or fault injection in README or analysis module
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: generate_current_vs_frequency_curve simulates a cell over a range of injected current amplitudes (F-I and subthreshold traces)
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: approximate firing rates, threshold current and spike times (via pyelectro); not a broad standardised feature library like eFEL
rows.protocol_optimization: no: tuning extra (Neurotune) optimises model parameters, not stimulation protocols
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: tooling, no evaluation of a detection method
rows.software: pyNeuroML https://github.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML (LGPL-3.0 per GitHub API; PyPI pyNeuroML 1.3.22, LGPL-3.0-only)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Execution and analysis substrate NeuroSem would reuse: current-step sweeps, and analyse_spiketime_vs_dt compares spike times across timesteps, a primitive for refinement-based tolerance calibration. NeuroSem adds reference-versus-transformed fingerprint comparison, mutant generation, frozen tolerances, battery selection and held-out evaluation.

rows.citation: NeuroML organisation (2012). NeuroML2: NeuroML 2 Schema, LEMS ComponentType definitions and core documentation [software]. GitHub.
rows.model_type: NeuroML 2 XML schema, LEMS ComponentType definitions and example cell/network models
rows.controlled_mutations: no: no fault injection; schema and examples only
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: each OMV test reuses the example's single fixed LEMS simulation; no stimulus battery per model
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: OMV tests compare threshold-detected spike times against stored expected values with per-observable tolerances
rows.software: NeuroML2 https://github.com/NeuroML/NeuroML2 (LGPL-3.0 per GitHub API); OMV test files reference OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Hosts the schema used for structural validity and the canonical saved-spike-time regression tests (82 .omt files) across engines such as jNeuroML, NEURON, NetPyNE, EDEN. This is essentially NeuroSem's canonical baseline; NeuroSem adds multi-protocol fingerprints, mutants surviving these checks, battery selection and held-out evaluation.
